title: Answer to Question: What Lies Behind the Trilateral Summit in Azerbaijan!
text:
Answer to Question

What Lies Behind the Trilateral Summit in Azerbaijan!

Question: On Monday 8/8/2016, for the first time, a trilateral summit was held bringing together the presidents of Russia, Iran and Azerbaijan in Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan. The final statement mentioned several topics that were discussed, such as relations between the three states, economic cooperation and the North-South Corridor, combating terrorism, the Syrian crisis, Afghanistan, drug trafficking, extremism, cross-border crime, illegal arms trafficking, human trafficking... etc., and all of this in one day! So is it for media propaganda, or is there a topic that was focused upon and the rest is embellishment? Furthermore, Iran and Azerbaijan go along with American policy, so does America have a role in this meeting? And if so, what is its aim in that?

Answer: Yes, it is not reasonable that all this wide spectrum of topics be focused upon in one or two sessions, and in one day or part of a day! But it appears that the economic topic is the aim of this summit, especially the establishment of the economic corridor called the (North-South Corridor)... and that America has the fundamental role in this, which is to distance Russia from China and to exhaust it economically by occupying it with this corridor from Russia to Azerbaijan, then Iran and the Gulf... To clarify this, we review the following matters:

First: The other matters mentioned in the final statement are not of consequence for a summit meeting... We detail them as follows:

1- As for Afghanistan, none of these three states has any say in the matter of Afghanistan; rather, the influential and active state there is America, for it is dominant over the government of Afghanistan. Therefore its mention in the statement is among the side matters...!

2- As for cross-border crime and human trafficking, these are not among the priorities of common concern of the mentioned states such that a summit would be held for them...

3- As for the Syrian crisis, Russia and Iran need to coordinate with each other regarding Syria to avoid defeat there, but the fact that Azerbaijan has no role in the Syrian crisis makes the holding of the summit not for this purpose, especially as Azerbaijan is the one that called for the summit: (It is notable that this trilateral meeting, held today, Monday, is the first in this format, which the Azerbaijani president proposed during a telephone call he made with his Russian counterpart last February.) (Source: i24news, 8/8/2016). This means that the summit which Azerbaijan called for would not be for the Syrian crisis, since Azerbaijan has no role in it.

4- As for combating terrorism, drugs and the transit of weapons and armed men, especially between Azerbaijan and Russia as a corridor for the Mujahideen to the Caucasus, as was the case during the Chechen wars throughout the decade of the nineties of the twentieth century... Although Russia mentioned it at the summit, as Russia Today reported on 8/8/2016: "President Vladimir Putin, during his trilateral meeting with his Iranian counterpart Hassan Rouhani and his Azerbaijani counterpart Ilham Aliyev, stressed the necessity of confronting the transit of militants, weapons and drugs through the three states. And President Putin on Monday 8 August called for activating the exchange of information between the three states about the activity of terrorist organisations," such matters are ones that Russia can settle bilaterally with Azerbaijan without the need for a summit that includes the Iranian president. The issue of the "transit of militants and weapons" is a Russian-Azerbaijani problem, because the passage of "militants" is usually through Azerbaijan... As for the drugs coming from Afghanistan through Iran and Azerbaijan, its topic, even if it has an effect, does not have priority for these states in the current circumstances such that a summit would be held for it...

Second: Thus the previous matters, even if they have an effect, are not a reason for holding a summit between the three states... What remains is the economic topic, which is the main aim of holding this summit, especially the establishment of the economic corridor (the North-South Corridor)... To clarify this, we set out what came in the statement about the economic matters, as well as the statements made on this subject:

1- It came in the final statement: (Russia, Iran and Azerbaijan decided to take measures to develop transport infrastructure, including the development of the "North-South" corridor, as the three parties seek to make efforts with the aim of integrating regional transport capability, aimed at establishing infrastructure for economic, profitable and environmentally safe transport... And the three states intend to take steps to develop transport infrastructure with the aim of improving the current capabilities for transporting passengers and goods through the international "North-South" transport corridor... The statement also noted that Moscow, Tehran and Baku continue together "to contribute to the implementation of new projects to connect railway lines, within the plans to develop and improve the efficiency of the international 'North-South' transport corridor"...) (Russia Today, 9/8/2016)

2- The statement of the Iranian President Rouhani about the aim of the conference, saying: "strengthening wide-ranging development opportunities between these states" (Al-Alam channel website, 8/8/2016).

3- What the Russian media reported about the most prominent aims of the conference: (The Russian news agency Sputnik on 8/8/2016 spoke about a huge Russian-Iranian project competing with the Egyptian Suez Canal, and the Russian agency stated: "Among the most important topics to be raised at the summit is the establishment of an international corridor linking the north and the south, so that this project competes with the Egyptian Suez Canal to some extent, as the length of the corridor is 7,200 kilometres, and it links northern Europe with India and the Gulf states through Iran, Russia and Azerbaijan. And the Iranian Foreign Minister announced that this project will serve the interests of the peoples of Iran, Azerbaijan and Russia and the interests of the entire region, as the project will provide an effective alternative, in terms of cost and time, to the sea route through the Suez Canal").

4- Likewise, Russia Today mentioned on 8/8/2016 that (the Russian President affirmed before the summit was held that trilateral cooperation between Russia, Iran and Azerbaijan will allow the implementation of a number of new projects in the Caspian region. Putin said: "Before us are many topics put forward for discussion in the trilateral format"...)

Thus the fundamental aim of this conference is economic cooperation, especially the North-South Corridor, and it takes precedence over the economic projects on the Caspian Sea, because the remaining states on this sea were not invited to the summit. Therefore, the discussion of this topic at the summit conference was not for actual implementation so much as it is a future discussion, and it may be distant until an understanding is reached with the other states bordering the sea. As for the corridor, it concerns the three states, especially as the Russian media highlighted it and that it will compete with the Suez Canal...

Third: As for the American role, it is indeed present, and part of it does not require depth of thought, while part of it requires reflection and depth... As for the first part, it can be easily understood from the fact that these three states differ in their reality: Russia is an independent state with its own regional and international policies, while Iran and Azerbaijan are two states that go along with American policy, and the foreign policy of such states is not separate from American policy. In other words, the establishment of a corridor from the north to the south as far as the Gulf on the shores of Iran is not separate from American policy. This is in respect of the first part, which can be easily understood without depth of thought. As for the second part, which requires depth and reflection, it can be understood by taking the following matters into account:

1- America noticed the difficult economic situation of Russia, so it ordered Azerbaijan and Iran to entice Russia with a large economic project that exhausts the Russian economy... And just as is America's policy on the Chinese side, of occupying it with spending on huge projects such as the Chinese economic corridor through Pakistan, America likewise wants to push Russia to spend on the new "North-South" corridor so as to exhaust its economy and force it into the debts of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, over which America dominates. For the sake of all this, it ordered Iran and Azerbaijan to also spend on this "corridor" project to encourage Russia to go forward and engage in it.

2- At the time when America is intensifying its policies in the Far East to prevent China from becoming a prominent global power, and is stirring up hotspots of tension around China, it certainly realises that the most dangerous aspect of the Russian orientation towards Asia is Russia's orientation towards China. And if America's policy is based on isolating China from strengthening itself with the other major states, it certainly realises that Russia is the most dangerous of those states in the matter of rapprochement with China. Within the framework of distancing Russia from China, it entices it with such a "North-South" corridor, especially as this economic corridor crossing Azerbaijan and Russia is like the twin of the Indian-Iranian economic corridor, which connects India by sea with Iran at the Iranian port of Chabahar and likewise links Iran with Afghanistan by land. That is, the new "North-South" corridor crossing Russia gives more vitality to the Indian economic corridor by linking it with northern Europe, so that Russia appears alongside India, the traditional enemy of China in South Asia, thereby separating them. On the other hand, Russia's integration into this economic corridor with Iran and Azerbaijan will certainly limit Russia's integration with the Chinese plans for economic corridors, such as the "Silk Road" corridor... In sum, America sees a worrying orientation of Russia towards China, so it pushes its followers in Iran and Azerbaijan to entice Russia with joint projects with them, so that Russia turns away from China and China turns away from it.

Fourth: The conclusion is:

1- The aim of the trilateral summit in Baku on 8/8/2016 is an economic aim, especially the North-South Corridor.

2- America has an influential role in the summit through Azerbaijan and Iran, by bringing Russia into the North-South Corridor project, in order to exhaust the Russian economy during its current crisis and to push Russia to be occupied with projects in the direction of south-west of Russia, to Azerbaijan and then Iran, instead of the direction of south-east of Russia towards China, and consequently to isolate Russia from China gradually.

11th of Dhul Qi'dah 1437 AH

14/8/2016 CE
